fact_check.claim: New students ride TCAT free for their first year with the Cornell ID card
fact_check.note: Page: bus fare is free for the first year for all new students, with Cornell ID.

fact_check.claim: Fully subsidized passes go to students new to their program, including first-year transfer students; expire August 31 (fall entrants) and December 31 (spring entrants)
fact_check.note: Wording now matches the source (previous fix applied).

fact_check.claim: After the first year, free TCAT after 6 p.m. weekdays and any time on weekends
fact_check.note: Source: free unlimited rides after 6 p.m. weekdays and all day weekends.

fact_check.claim: Other students can buy discounted bus passes and OmniRide privileges at myparking.cornell.edu; prices not given
fact_check.note: Source mentions discounted passes via myparking.cornell.edu and no prices.

fact_check.claim: Doctoral students and graduate assistants get free OmniRide passes (undergraduates should not count on them)
fact_check.note: Source: all registered doctoral students and graduate assistants are eligible for free Omniride passes. The who-gets-what line is present near the top of the section.

fact_check.claim: Short Line: 15% off every day; trip must start or end in the town on the ID; one reduced ticket per student; buy at a terminal; online available for Cornell and Ithaca College
fact_check.note: All supported. Page lists online purchase for several other schools too, but the article does not say Cornell and Ithaca are the only ones. No dollar fares on page, as the article says.

fact_check.claim: C2C: students with NetID pay $93.50 one way or $187 round trip; public fare $101 / $202; saves $7.50 / $15; includes temporary $6 surcharge
fact_check.note: Fares and surcharge match; savings arithmetic is correct. Public fare is now stated (previous fix applied).

fact_check.claim: Cornell says students are eligible for discounted Ithaca Carshare memberships
fact_check.note: Source: Cornell students are eligible for discounted Ithaca Carshare memberships.

fact_check.claim: Carshare says Cornell helps subsidize annual memberships through the Commuter Alternative Program
fact_check.note: Source says Cornell subsidizes annual memberships through the Commuter Alternative Program.

fact_check.claim: $45 discount on both annual plans (Just In Case $30/yr, $9/hr; It's My Car $310/yr, $6/hr; 42 cents/mile cars)
fact_check.note: Table matches, $45 discount on both (previous fix applied); used in the at-a-glance table.

fact_check.claim: One-time nonrefundable $20 fee per driver per application; sales and rental taxes apply; monthly plans get no student discount
fact_check.note: Source: $20 fee, 8% sales tax and 12% rental tax on hourly and mileage charges, monthly plans no discount.

fact_check.claim: Johnson Museum admission free for everyone; Tue-Fri 10-5, Sat-Sun noon-4, closed Mondays, closed November 25-27
fact_check.note: All match the visit page.

fact_check.claim: Anabel's is in Anabel Taylor Hall, Room 127; hours noon-7 Wed-Fri, noon-3 Sat
fact_check.note: Official site lists these hours and location; article advises confirming since posts are undated (previous fix applied).

fact_check.claim: Anabel's runs during the academic year and accepts SNAP; November 10, 2025 update: reduced prices on ten staples and 50% off for all customers, due to government shutdown, dated, check Anabel's site; not confirmed still running
fact_check.note: Cornell Health page says exactly this and says to check the site. Article correctly frames it as not a standing discount.

fact_check.claim: Anabel's site does not state a standing student discount
fact_check.note: No standing discount listed on the site.

fact_check.claim: Cornell Health advice: compare prices, rewards programs, generic brands, coupons, check SNAP; names no stores
fact_check.note: Matches the money-saving tips list.

fact_check.claim: Free or discounted Cornell Music concerts, Schwartz Center tickets, Cornell Cinema and Cinemapolis tickets, discounted men's hockey tickets; no prices; list written for grad students
fact_check.note: All listed on the page, no prices.

fact_check.claim: Big Red Sports Pass for most Cornell sports
fact_check.note: Source: unlimited access except men's hockey; 'most' is consistent (previous fix applied).

fact_check.claim: Free equipment loans from Cornell Recreation, open lap swimming at Helen Newman and Teagle, discounted Outdoor Education classes
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: The Cornell Store discounts technology and cell products
fact_check.note: Matches; the 'three locations' claim was removed (previous fix applied).

fact_check.claim: 2014 Downtown Ithaca Alliance student card: 10, 15 or 20 percent off at 34 businesses, Cornell and four other local schools; no current list found
fact_check.note: Source: fall 2014 launch, 34 businesses, 10/15/20 percent, five schools in total. Article dated and hedged as a lead, not a current discount.

fact_check.claim: Nearly a third of students use TCAT as their main way to get to campus (Reed Huegerich, assistant director of transportation)
fact_check.note: Source says nearly a third use TCAT as their primary mode; attributed to the author's stated role. Not a hard-fact dependency on student voice.

beats_top.query: how to save money at Cornell student discounts Ithaca
beats_top.why: The top result is a graduate-student-only list with no prices, no eligibility detail and no transport numbers. Ours opens with the answer, gives dollar and percent figures (Carshare $45, C2C $7.50/$15, Short Line 15%), says who qualifies for each TCAT perk, and flags what could not be verified.
changes: Optional: add TCAT pass prices if myparking.cornell.edu publishes them.
Optional: add Cornell Cinema and Cinemapolis student ticket prices if an official page lists them.
